_grouping: ⭐ FOUR NAMES IN ONE ADD, under item 7's split rule. That rule says separate a RISKY arity so it cannot take the others down — `math.pi` is a constant and `math.ceil`/`math.floor`/`year` are names that certainly exist, so none of these four could sink the others. `alma` (a v3-era bare spelling that may not exist in v6), `ta.nvi`, `ta.correlation` and `ta.percentile_linear_interpolation` were deliberately EXCLUDED for that reason.

math.pi.verdict: IEEE-754 double π, constant on every one of the 400 bars.
math.pi._: ⭐ There was no vendor QUESTION here — it is π — but there was a vendor CONFIRMATION, which is different. A table row is now backed by the vendor's own constant rather than by arithmetic we already believed.

math.ceil._: ⚠️ THE NEGATIVE IS THE ONLY INFORMATIVE READ, and it happens to AGREE with toward-zero: both give -2. So `ceil` alone cannot separate the two rules — it is `floor` below that does, and the two must be pinned as a PAIR from one reading.

math.floor._: ⭐⭐ THE DISCRIMINATING READ OF THE PAIR. Toward-zero would have answered -2. -3 settles it: both functions go toward ±∞, which is what JS `Math.ceil`/`Math.floor` and Python `math.ceil`/`math.floor` do natively — so neither needs the hand-written correction `round` does (Pine rounds a half AWAY FROM ZERO, which is neither lane's default).

year._: ⭐⭐ SETTLED BY `hour`, NOT BY `year`, AND THE PROBE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN COMMENT. `year` disagrees between the two clocks only across a New Year boundary, so on 11 September it cannot answer its own question. `hour` disagrees EVERY day and reads the SAME clock. The daily bar stamped 1789047000 is 09:30 ET / 13:30 UTC, and `hour` read 9 — so the clock is the exchange's, and `year` rides on that. The 400 bars spanning 2025 and 2026 are the sanity check that `year` varies at all.

_what_the_door_did_before_this_capture._: ⛔ MEASURED THROUGH `translatePine(src, {strict:true})`, not assumed. `r11-remaining-nine.md` lists `year` as one of the nine needing a vendor read before it can be added — but it is ALREADY SERVED: the closed table declares it in its `clock` section and `clockLeaf` binds it. So item 8's row 3 needs no engine work at all; what the capture bought there is the TIMEZONE, which the backlog correctly said was unknown.

_bounds: ⚠️ ONE SYMBOL, ONE TIMEFRAME, ONE DAY. AMEX:SPY, 1D, chart session `regular`, 2026-09-11. `math.ceil`/`math.floor` were read at two literal inputs (-2.5 and 2.5); a half-integer is the case that separates the rounding rules, but nothing here reads a non-half fraction, an infinity, or `na`. The `year` timezone is inferred from `hour` on the same clock family rather than observed across a New Year boundary — which is the only direct test and is four months away.
